question: In infants and young children with cardiac failure, hepatomegaly is a more reliable sign of right heart failure than ankle oedema, because the hepatic venous bed is more compliant and dependent than the peripheral tissues at this age.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Do not apply adult failure criteria to infants. In an infant lying flat, ankle oedema does not accumulate; the liver enlarges visibly and palpably when right heart pressures rise. Hepatomegaly is the key sign to seek on examination.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Ankle oedema — the hallmark of right heart failure in adults — is unreliable in infants who are recumbent most of the time. The liver distends readily with venous congestion and is detectable on examination. Hepatomegaly is therefore the most important sign of right-sided failure in infants. Other age-specific features include feeding difficulty, tachypnoea, and periorbital oedema.
